title: How Do Label Errors Affect Thin Crack Detection by DNNs
mechanism: Label cracks as 1 px curves with matching training and evaluation, then synthesise annotation errors: under-annotation hurts more than over-annotation; polyline approximation has modest impact.
adaptation: Benchmark: score crack as curves (relF1 on skeletons) and add a label-error robustness column (train on CV labels with synthetic 1 px jitter and 20% dropped segments). Model side: favour recall when refining labels; polyline-simplified labels are acceptable targets.
min_experiment: For the top 5 suite methods, one extra CV training on corrupted labels; report drop in CV relF1@2; no kill line (measurement).
evidence: Synthetic error study on 1 px curve labels; qualitative findings in abstract; numbers not read.

alt_notes.adaptation: Design rule for every refinement arm: never delete crack label pixels that cannot be placed on a ridge; benchmark should report recall-oriented tolerant metrics alongside strict IoU, and can repeat the error-synthesis study on EL labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark study: add synthetic under-annotation (drop 10% of components) and 1 px jitter to train labels, train house 3 seeds each, measure crack IoU and relF1@2 drop. Kill: not a method; stop if drops are under 0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our dotted, thin-traced crack labels behave like under-annotation; train on labels dilated by 1 px (or an asymmetric soft band) and score on the original labels with a val-chosen bias.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm 1 px-dilated crack labels vs SUP100, 5 v 5. Kill if crack IoU (original labels, val bias) < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.

alt_notes.adaptation: Our dotted, under-traced crack labels are under-annotation; train on 1 px dilated crack labels or a soft band, score on original labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: crack labels dilated by 1 px, 5 seeds; baseline SUP100. Kill: crack IoU on original labels < +0.012 or relP@2 drop > 0.05.
